documents.title: Follow-up, post-chemotherapy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Four months out from BR, PET in October showed complete response. Energy most of the way back; walking again. No fevers, sweats, lumps.
Heart: no palpitations, breathing fine. Cardiology surveillance due in March.
Kidneys: no flank pain lately.
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25. NKDA.

Exam: BP 139/64, HR 62. No cervical/supraclavicular/axillary nodes. Diastolic murmur LSB, regular rhythm. Lungs clear. Flanks full. No edema.

A/P
1. Follicular lymphoma in CR - oncology surveillance q6 mo.
2. HTN with AR/ascending aneurysm - systolic above the 130 goal; home log, he'll send it.
3. ADPKD - CMP today; nephrology due this year.
4. Vaccines: Shingrix #1 and PCV20 today (post-chemo). Shingrix #2 in 2 months.
5. Lipids today.

documents.title: January labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glenn - kidney function steady (creatinine in your usual range), potassium and liver tests normal. Triglycerides and LDL about where they've always been. Second shingles shot in March - the front desk will send a reminder.

documents.title: Shingrix #2
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Shingrix dose 2 IM L deltoid. Dose 1 caused a sore arm and a tired day. Series complete.

events.reason: surveillance of aortic regurgitation and ascending aortic aneurysm

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness. LVEF 55-60%. Normal right ventricle. Trileaflet aortic valve with moderate aortic regurgitation, similar to 02/2024. No stenosis. Ascending aorta 4.6 cm. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Moderate aortic regurgitation, stable. Normal LV size and function, LVEF 55-60%. Ascending aorta 4.6 cm.

documents.title: Cardiology surveillance
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology, 03/26/2025.
Asymptomatic; exercising. Completed lymphoma therapy (BR, no anthracycline) last fall, in remission. No palpitations since ablation.
Meds: lisinopril 20, hydrochlorothiazide 25. NKDA.
Echo today: normal LV size, EF 55-60%; moderate AR, unchanged; ascending aorta 4.6 cm (4.5 previously, within measurement variability).
Impression: moderate AR with normal LV; ascending aortic aneurysm 4.6 cm, stable; recovered tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.
Plan: continue BP control, goal under 130/80. Repeat echo in one year. Return sooner for dyspnea, chest or back pain.

documents.title: Cardiology letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cardiology surveillance reviewed: moderate AR stable, EF 55-60%, ascending aorta 4.6 cm. Repeat in a year. No changes.

documents.title: Lymphoma surveillance
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body: Surveillance visit 04/22/2025, seven months after completing BR for stage III follicular lymphoma. Feels well, no B symptoms. No palpable adenopathy or splenomegaly. CBC normal; LDH 194. Remains in complete remission. Next visit in 6 months.

documents.title: Refill: lisinopril, HCTZ
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request for 90-day lisinopril 20 mg and HCTZ 25 mg. Seen 1/2025, BMP 1/2025. Sent per protocol, 1 refill. Physical booked 7/22.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
50M annual. Good year after a hard one. Back to full days in the office; walking 4-5 days/wk. Alcohol a couple of drinks a week. Sleeping well.
Problems: HTN; ADPKD; moderate AR with 4.6 cm ascending aneurysm (cardiology 3/2025, stable); flutter s/p ablation with recovered EF; follicular lymphoma in CR (onc 4/2025); psychogenic ED (not raised today).
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25. NKDA.
PHQ-9 2. AUDIT-C 2.

Exam: BP 131/67, HR 62. Normal general exam. No adenopathy. Diastolic murmur LSB, unchanged. Lungs clear. Abdomen: bilateral flank fullness. Skin: no concerning lesions. No edema.

A/P
1. HTN - at the edge of goal. Continue; keep home log.
2. ADPKD - CMP, UA today; nephrology appointment for the fall.
3. Health maintenance: colonoscopy 2021 normal (next 2031). Shingrix done, PCV20 done. Tdap 2018. Flu/COVID in the fall.
4. AR/aneurysm, lymphoma - specialist surveillance as scheduled.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All good: blood counts normal, kidney function stable, potassium normal, urine without protein or blood.

documents.title: Lymphoma surveillance
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body: Surveillance 10/21/2025, 13 months after BR. Asymptomatic. Exam without adenopathy or organomegaly. CBC normal, LDH 207. Continued complete remission. Return April 2026.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 2025-26 flu and COVID vaccines given. No reactions last year. Observed 15 min, fine.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Nephrology follow-up 11/12/2025 (last seen here 04/2021).
Interval: atrial flutter ablated 2023 with recovered EF; moderate AR and 4.6 cm ascending aneurysm under cardiology surveillance; follicular lymphoma treated 2024, in remission. Kidneys: occasional mild flank ache, no hematuria, no infections.
Meds: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. NKDA.
Creatinine 1.27 today, slowly drifting up from about 1.2. BP in clinic acceptable.
Assessment: ADPKD with mildly reduced, slowly declining function; hypertension acceptably controlled.
Plan: continue current medicines, fluids, avoid NSAIDs. BMP with primary care labs. Return in one year.

documents.title: Nephrology letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Nephrology note reviewed: ADPKD, creatinine 1.27, slow drift. Continue current regimen. Labs with us at next visit.

documents.title: Refill: lisinopril, HCTZ
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 90-day lisinopril 20 / HCTZ 25 sent. BMP 11/2025 at nephrology reviewed - K and creatinine fine.

reports.text: Noncontrast CT of the head. Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage filling the basal cisterns and extending along the anterior interhemispheric fissure. No intraparenchymal hematoma. Ventricles normal in size; no hydrocephalus. No midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Calvarium intact.
reports.conclusion: Acute subarachnoid hemorrhage in the basal cisterns and anterior interhemispheric fissure. No hydrocephalus.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency Department Record - received from community hospital ED
Date of visit: 03/14/2026

CC: sudden severe headache.

HPI: 51-year-old man with ADPKD and a history of headaches, brought in by his wife about 2 hours after an abrupt headache he calls the worst of his life, with nausea and light sensitivity. No trauma. No anticoagulants.

PMH: ADPKD; hypertension; aortic regurgitation; tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy; psychogenic ED; adjustment disorder; non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; lisinopril. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: paternal grandfather died of a ruptured cerebral aneurysm at 58; father ADPKD.

Exam: BP 180/110. Alert but anxious. Neck stiff with nuchal rigidity. Pupils equal and reactive, no focal motor or sensory deficit, speech normal.

CT head: subarachnoid hemorrhage in the basal cisterns and anterior interhemispheric fissure, no hydrocephalus.
Labs: CBC, BMP unremarkable; INR 1.1.

ED course: IV antiemetic and analgesia, IV nicardipine for systolic under 160. Neurosurgery at the regional tertiary center accepted.
Impression: aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage until proven otherwise.
Disposition: transferred by critical care transport to the neuro-ICU.

conditions.label: Ruptured cerebral aneurysm
conditions.note: anterior communicating artery aneurysm, 7 mm, coiled 2026-03-15

medications.sig: Take 2 capsules (60 mg) by mouth every 4 hours for 21 days total (through 04/04/2026)

documents.title: Neurointerventional procedure report
documents.author: neurointerventional radiology
documents.body:
Neurointerventional Radiology - Procedure Report
Date: 03/15/2026
Procedure: diagnostic cerebral angiography and endovascular coil embolization of an anterior communicating artery aneurysm.
Indication: subarachnoid hemorrhage; CT angiography 03/14 demonstrating a 7 mm anterior communicating artery aneurysm.
Access: right common femoral artery, ultrasound guided, closure device.
Findings: 7 mm saccular aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery, the source of hemorrhage. No other aneurysm.
Treatment: coil embolization with near-complete occlusion. Parent vessels preserved. No thromboembolic complication.
Plan: neuro-ICU; follow-up angiogram at about 6 months.

documents.title: Neurosurgery discharge summary
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Regional tertiary center, Neurosciences ICU / Neurosurgery - Discharge Summary
Admitted 03/14/2026 (transfer from community ED); discharged 03/26/2026.

Diagnosis: aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from a ruptured 7 mm anterior communicating artery aneurysm, treated with endovascular coiling 03/15/2026.

Course: arrived alert, no focal deficits. CT angiography showed the aneurysm; coiled the next morning. Nimodipine started on admission. Blood pressure controlled with IV agents then his home lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. Daily transcranial Dopplers and neuro checks without clinically significant vasospasm; no hydrocephalus, no drain needed. Sodium stayed normal. Headache gradually improved. Ambulating independently; neurologically intact at discharge.

Discharge medications:
- nimodipine 60 mg by mouth every 4 hours to complete 21 days (last dose 04/04/2026)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily
- acetaminophen as needed for headache

Instructions: no driving or heavy lifting until reviewed in neurosurgery clinic. Blood pressure goal under 140/90 at first, ideally lower long term - primary care to follow. Neurosurgery clinic in 6-8 weeks; follow-up angiogram at 6 months. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records request faxed to the tertiary center neurosciences unit for admission 3/14-3/26/2026 (discharge summary, procedure reports). Patient signed release at front desk.

documents.title: Home from the hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's wife called: Glenn home since yesterday after 12 days at the tertiary center for a brain bleed from an aneurysm, coiled. Headache 3/10, taking nimodipine every 4 hours on an alarm, BP at home 140s/90. No new weakness, speech fine. Booked with PCP Tue 3/31. Asked them to bring discharge papers; records requested from the hospital.

events.reason: follow-up after hospitalization for subarachnoid hemorrhage

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharge summary and angiography report received yesterday and reviewed.

SAH 3/14 from a ruptured 7 mm AComm aneurysm, coiled 3/15, 12 days in the neuro-ICU/floor without vasospasm or hydrocephalus. Home 3/26.
Now: headache 2-3/10, dull, much better each day. Mild fatigue. No weakness, numbness, vision or speech problems. Nimodipine q4h through 4/4 - tolerating, a bit lightheaded at times. Not driving; wife driving.
Meds: nimodipine 60 q4h (short course), lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP 146/88, repeat 144/86, HR 74. Alert, oriented, conversant, normal speech. Cranial nerves intact, strength 5/5 throughout, gait steady. Groin site clean. Diastolic murmur LSB, regular. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Aneurysmal SAH s/p coiling - recovering well. Neurosurgery clinic in May, follow-up angiogram ~September.
2. HTN - above goal after the bleed and with his aorta. Adding amlodipine 5 mg daily now; will watch for lightheadedness while nimodipine overlaps (ends 4/4) - he'll sit/stand slowly. Home BP twice daily, send in 2 wks. Goal under 130/80.
3. ADPKD - BMP today.
4. Lymphoma surveillance in April, cardiology echo due.
RTC 2 mo, sooner prn.

documents.title: Visit summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: New medicine: amlodipine 5 mg once daily. Finish nimodipine as prescribed through 4/4. Check your blood pressure morning and evening and send readings in 2 weeks; goal under 130/80. Stand up slowly. Call 911 for a sudden severe headache, weakness, numbness, trouble speaking or confusion.

documents.title: Labs from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sodium, potassium and kidney function all fine. Start the amlodipine as planned and send home readings in two weeks.

documents.title: BP log
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Done with the nimodipine 4/4. Two weeks on amlodipine: mornings 126-134 / 74-80, evenings a little lower. No more lightheadedness. Headaches only occasional now.

documents.title: RE: BP log
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Those are good numbers, Glenn - right where we want them. Stay on all three. See you in June.

documents.title: Lymphoma surveillance
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body: Surveillance 04/21/2026, 19 months after BR. Interval subarachnoid hemorrhage 03/2026, coiled, recovering. No B symptoms; fatigue attributed to recent hospitalization. No adenopathy or splenomegaly. CBC normal, LDH 199. Complete remission continues. Next visit in 6 months, then yearly.

events.reason: follow-up after coiled anterior communicating artery aneurysm

documents.title: Neurosurgery clinic follow-up
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Neurosurgery clinic, 05/12/2026.
Seven weeks after aneurysmal SAH from a 7 mm AComm aneurysm treated with coiling. Recovering well. Mild headaches a few times a week, relieved by acetaminophen, and some end-of-day fatigue. No focal symptoms. Back to work part-time from home. BP well controlled on lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine added by his PCP.
Exam: neurologically intact.
Plan: cleared to drive and return to usual activity, avoiding heavy straining for another month. Follow-up catheter angiogram planned for September 2026 to assess the coil mass. Continue strict BP control. NKDA.

events.reason: follow-up: blood pressure, recovery after subarachnoid hemorrhage

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About 12 weeks after SAH/coiling. Neurosurgery cleared him to drive in May. Headaches down to once a week, mild. Energy improving, back in the office three days a week. Mood ok, PHQ-2 1. Home BP 120s-130/70s.
Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP 128/76, HR 68. Neuro nonfocal. Diastolic murmur LSB, regular. Lungs clear. Ankles without edema on amlodipine.

A/P
1. HTN - at goal on three drugs. Continue. BMP today.
2. SAH s/p coiling - follow-up angiogram in September per neurosurgery.
3. AR/ascending aneurysm - cardiology echo this summer.
4. Follicular lymphoma - in remission, oncology October.
5. ADPKD - nephrology November.
RTC September.

documents.title: Visit summary
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood pressure 128/76 - at goal. Keep taking amlodipine 5 mg, lisinopril 20 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. Blood test today; we'll message results. Next visit in September.

documents.title: June labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium and sodium normal on the three blood pressure medicines; creatinine 1.35, about where it was at nephrology last fall.

reports.text: Left ventricle normal in size, LVEF 55-60%. Normal RV. Trileaflet aortic valve with moderate aortic regurgitation, unchanged. Ascending aorta 4.6 cm, unchanged from 03/2025. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Stable moderate aortic regurgitation with normal LV size and function. Ascending aorta 4.6 cm, unchanged.

documents.title: Cardiology surveillance
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology, 07/21/2026.
Interval aneurysmal SAH in March, coiled; recovering. No cardiac symptoms.
Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 20, hydrochlorothiazide 25. NKDA.
BP 131/74. Echo: moderate AR, normal LV, EF 55-60%; ascending aorta 4.6 cm, unchanged.
Impression: stable moderate AR and ascending aortic aneurysm.
Plan: continue current regimen; repeat echo in 12 months.

documents.title: Cardiology note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cardiology 7/21 reviewed: AR moderate and aorta 4.6 cm, both stable. Nothing new for us. Will discuss at September visit.

documents.title: Refill: amlodipine, lisinopril, HCTZ
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 90-day supplies of amlodipine 5 mg, lisinopril 20 mg and HCTZ 25 mg sent. Seen 6/8, BMP 6/8 normal. Next visit 9/15.

documents.title: Angiogram
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Neurosurgery scheduled my follow-up angiogram for September 22. Do I need to stop any of my BP pills beforehand, or is that their call?

documents.title: RE: Angiogram
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Glenn - the angiography team will give you the instructions; usually blood pressure medicines are taken as normal with a sip of water. Please confirm with them at the pre-procedure call. We'll see you on 9/15.
